moments.title: A new West Side ballpark
moments.text: Chicago's National League club, the future Cubs, moved to a park on the block bounded by Polk, Lincoln (now Wolcott), Taylor and Wood streets. It held about 16,000 seats.

moments.title: World champions
moments.text: The Cubs won the World Series.

moments.title: Champions again
moments.text: The Cubs repeated as World Series champions. They would not win another title until 2016, 108 years later.

moments.title: The last game
moments.text: The Cubs beat St. Louis 7 to 2 in their final game at West Side Grounds, then moved to the North Side park now called Wrigley Field.

moments.title: Sold for a hospital
moments.text: The State of Illinois bought the site for $40,000 to build a research and teaching hospital, the start of today's Illinois Medical District.

moments.title: Today: the University of Illinois medical campus
moments.text: Nothing of the ballpark remains, but part of the old outfield is a park inside the medical complex. A historical marker stands at 912 S. Wood St, in front of the University of Illinois Hospital.

Address could be sharpened to Polk and Wood; the pin is within the old block.
